what: Once ticket 02 ships, an interventions change saved before this build where only the number of repeats moved will still appear as unread, and its card will read Removed None, Added None, with every name under Unchanged. The analyst is sent to a change that names nothing, which user story 18 rules out; the spec also says changes already saved are drawn the new way. Whether the owner's database holds such a change is unknown: I found no database in the repo to look. The cause is that ticket 01 stops new repeat-only changes being detected, but nothing filters the ones already saved, and its rule for counting distinct names (diff.py, inside _comparable) is written separately from the added/removed/unchanged split ticket 02 will add, so the two can drift apart. The named field set SPLIT is right for ticket 02 to reuse as the fields shown as added/removed. What ticket 02 should not copy is the second, private rule. It should have the split decide both questions: an interventions change counts as moved only when something was added or removed, applied when changes are detected and when saved changes are served. Fixing this now is one change; left alone, every field that later joins SPLIT carries two rules that must be kept in agreement.
